about: Amr's expansion scenes X001-X124: eight key poses each (sheets 1536 x 1024, eight 384 x 512 slots; slot 1 is a real beat, so all eight frames ship). From the refined expansion release of 13 November 2026 (Amr_Refined_Expansion_124.zip, catalog.json; docs/mascot/refined-expansion-release.json). scripts/build-expansion-spec.py writes this file, engine/expansion-table.ts and engine/expansion-titles.ts; scripts/build-mascot-expansion.py builds the packs as drawn. Each sheet's trigger and loop are the release's own rules: a scene may play only on the real event its trigger names, or when the visitor asks for it. docs/mascot/expansion-triggers.md records where each one plays. A sheet with `last` ends, and holds, on that beat: its later beats are drawn wrong (`last_why`).

He tilts the track toward his left, elbows moving asymmetrically, and watches the marble roll smoothly around the first broad lobe.
He twists his wrists to bring the second groove down, guiding the marble through its wide return curve with an interested half-smile.
He turns the pinched third groove downward; the marble stops visibly before the narrow section and his smile becomes a puzzled small O.
He crouches slightly and raises the track closer to eye level, looking along the blocked groove from its side.
His right thumb gently presses the outside of the pinched section while his left hand steadies it; he identifies the drag without forcing the marble through.
He levels the track and rolls the marble back into the open central basin, withdrawing the pressure with a considered nod.
He holds the track diagonally across his waist, the pinched groove visible and his free palm open beside it, ready to discuss that one fix.

sheets.title: Treat the error budget as finite
sheets.purpose: Make consumed reliability allowance and remaining reserve physically distinct, and show restraint when the reserve shrinks.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative SLO Builder preview, or after a confirmed burn event is recorded. The vessel is a metaphor, not a live reliability gauge.
sheets.loop: Hold frame8. Do not refill or reset the vessel inside the animation; a replay is an explicitly illustrative restart, never recovered service or budget.
props: One sealed flat transparent two-chamber vessel, about90px tall and60px wide at native scale, with a broad amber divider and one captive sliding gate. The shallow internal depth permits exactly one visible layer, with no beads hidden behind others. Exactly three large teal discs remain inside the vessel in every pose: initially two above the divider and one below; after one transfer, one above and two below. The three discs never leave, multiply or disappear.

slots.beat: Amr holds the flat transparent vessel upright at waist height in both hands. Exactly three separated large teal discs are clearly visible: two in the upper reserve chamber, one in the lower spent chamber. He looks down carefully.
He raises the same vessel toward his chest and tilts his head to inspect it, keeping its broad flat face toward the viewer. The same two upper discs and one lower disc remain separately visible.
His left palm supports the lower chamber and his right thumb grips the captive gate. He levels the vessel with a focused expression; exactly two discs are still above and one below.

He slides the gate open and tips the vessel slightly: one disc stays clearly in the upper chamber, one disc is visibly passing through the open divider, and the original spent disc stays below. Exactly three discs total.

He levels the vessel and closes the gate after the transfer. One clearly visible disc now remains above the divider and two separately visible discs rest side by side below; both hands still support the vessel.

He lifts the vessel slightly in his right hand while his left hand raises exactly one counting finger beside it. The flat face stays toward the viewer: one upper disc and two lower discs, exactly the same three total.

He supports the vessel with his left palm and raises his right hand into a deliberate pause gesture beside the closed gate. One upper reserve disc and two lower spent discs remain clearly visible and separated.

He cradles the closed vessel near his waist with both hands and settles into a sober measured stance. The final vessel still shows exactly one disc above and two discs below, with no refill, disappearing disc or celebration.

sheets.title: Choose the support that needs investment
sheets.purpose: Explain platform maturity as the experience of the whole span, and mark a weak support for investment without pretending the platform is already mature.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Platform Engineering Maturity preview or after a confirmed assessment snapshot; not a claimed engineering repair.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8. The wedge remains a visible planning aid; never transform all supports into an improved maturity score.
props: One compact torso-width hand-held bridge model, about110px wide at native scale, with eight thick integral supports each at least10px broad; one orange support is shorter and its adjacent deck section hinges slightly.
One broad orange triangular temporary wedge.

slots.beat: Amr holds the bridge horizontally with both palms under its ends, the large orange wedge retained beneath his left thumb at the left end, looking down at the uneven span.
He raises his left end a little and looks beneath the deck, revealing the short orange support near the middle.
He lowers one fingertip gently onto the hinged deck over that support; the small sag makes him purse his lips in recognition.
He releases the deck, transfers the bridge to his left palm and takes the large orange wedge from beneath his left thumb with his right hand.
He places the wedge beneath the short support, maintaining visible contact with the bridge and keeping the wedge external and obviously temporary.
He gently retests the deck with a right fingertip while the wedge supports it, watching closely instead of celebrating.
He removes his fingertip and tilts the model frontward to show both the weak orange support and its temporary brace.
He lowers the braced model to waist height and opens his right hand toward the wedge, calmly proposing where the next investment belongs.

sheets.title: Keep the incident sequence clear
sheets.purpose: Show an incident lead building a chronological record and preserving the current point while the incident remains active.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Incident Commander preview or after a confirmed timeline entry is logged. Never indicate resolved service or sent communications from merely opening the tool.
sheets.loop: Hold the active-incident stance in frame 8. A new confirmed timeline event can restart the reel action; completion is not inferred.
props: One small hand reel containing a broad cream strip with three large spaced pictogram events, a red triangle at the newest event and an integral rewind knob; no text or timestamps.
One wide orange retaining clip.

slots.beat: Amr holds the reel in his left hand at his hip with the orange retaining clip parked on its upper rim, and the loose strip end in his right, alert and looking toward the red newest-event triangle.
He steps his right foot slightly back and pulls the strip horizontally across his waist so its three event symbols separate clearly.
He lifts the newest-event end toward his chest and bends his head down, scrutinizing the red triangle with an intent expression.
He lowers the strip to keep it taut and traces back along the sequence with his right thumb, never pointing at an external board.
He supports the strip across his left fingers, folds a short tail behind the newest event and lifts the orange clip off the reel rim with his right hand.
He closes the clip immediately after the red event to retain the current point, supporting the reel steadily in his other hand.
He turns the reel knob slightly to take up slack, leaving all three events and the newest red triangle visible across a short span.
He holds the preserved strip close to his torso in a steady ready stance, focused and attentive; no resolved badge or celebratory gesture.

sheets.title: Several conditions made one failure path
sheets.purpose: Show that several contributing conditions can align into one failure path, giving a blameless review a concrete system-level explanation.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Blameless Post-Mortem preview or after a confirmed post-mortem save. This physical model explains contributing conditions; it does not claim that a service was repaired.
sheets.loop: Hold frame8 on the understood pattern. Replaying the physical model never implies a real incident reoccurred or that a mitigation was implemented.
props: One compact set of exactly three plain cream discs, each about35px across at native scale and with one permanent round through-hole about16px across. The holes are physical transparent openings in every pose and on both sides. No emblems, stickers, shutters or filled centres. Three short blue edge tethers retain the discs by their outer rims only; there is no axial spine, spindle or bar through their centres.
One unchanged thick blunt red demonstration rod with a broad rounded end, about8px across at native scale, narrow enough to pass through the permanent holes.

slots.beat: Amr holds the three plain perforated discs loosely stacked in his left palm and the red rod low in his right hand. Three separate cream edges and the broad permanent front hole are visible; short blue edge tethers retain the stack.

He fans the three tethered discs apart using his right thumb while retaining the rod across his curled right fingers. Every plain disc now has its own unmistakable open round hole; no hole contains a face emblem or central spindle.
He turns the front disc slightly by its outer rim and leans closer to inspect the same permanent open hole; the other two holed discs stay supported in his left palm, connected only at their edges.
He brings the three discs into a short parallel stack, aligning their existing round holes into one clear path. His left palm supports all three and the edge tethers hang away from the holes.

He pushes the unchanged red rod through all three permanent holes using his right hand. The far red end emerges beyond the third disc, while the plain cream rims and the open gaps around the rod remain visible.

He spreads the three discs slightly along the red rod with his left fingers, showing three separate plain cream rims and three separate holes around the same rod; the outer edge tethers remain slack and visible.
He withdraws the red rod completely into his right hand. All three round holes remain open and unchanged, and his left palm still supports the three discs joined by their outer edge tethers.

He presents the three spaced plain holed discs on his left palm and the removed red rod horizontally in his right. He settles into a calm thoughtful nod at the shared failure path; all three holes are still visibly open.

sheets.title: Share the rotation and notice load
sheets.purpose: Make the active shift and accumulated page load visible before a careful handoff; no assumption that a rotation removes burnout.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative On-Call Roster preview or after a confirmed rotation/page entry. Do not claim a person was contacted or a shift actually reassigned.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8 as a planning illustration. Actual rota ownership must come from a confirmed service event, and old load dots never vanish.
props: One short six-sided rotation drum with one blue-circle sector and one orange heavily marked sector, each represented by a few large dots; an integral flat docking lip sits above each sector.
One small dark pager-shaped block with an orange triangular face pictogram, no screen text.

slots.beat: Amr holds the rotation drum upright in his left palm with the pager docked above the heavily dotted orange sector, his eyes lowered toward it.
He brings the drum closer to his chest and turns his head slightly right, noticing the concentration of large page dots.
He tilts the drum so the orange sector faces him more directly, his free hand hovering beside the pager in a measured pause.
He lifts the pager off its dock with his right hand while his left keeps the loaded orange sector visible.
He rotates the drum one face toward a less dotted blue sector, keeping the pager visibly separate in his other hand.
He lowers the pager onto the blue sector’s docking lip as a demonstrated handoff plan, pressing gently until supported.
He cups both props at waist height and looks back to the still-visible orange sector, acknowledging the prior load rather than erasing it.
He turns slightly toward the viewer and holds the drum steady with the pager supported, his right palm open in a calm invitation to check the rotation together.

sheets.title: Dry-run every step, including the last
sheets.purpose: Show that runbook quality comes from following the whole procedure and exposing the step that cannot be executed, not merely owning a document.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Runbook Maturity preview or after a confirmed test entry. The practice mechanism never claims tested production recovery.
sheets.loop: Hold frame8 with the loose final grip exposed. Do not complete the crank motion or convert an untested runbook into a passed recovery test.
props: One compact cream triangular practice hub, about100px across, with three broad captive folding grips: blue circle, cream triangle and orange square. The first two grip hinges hold firm; the orange hinge visibly droops. Each grip is at least18px broad, no writing.

slots.beat: Amr holds the triangular procedure hub in his left palm at waist height, its three broad grips folded against the hub, looking down with a practical ready expression.
He unfolds the blue circle grip with his right fingers until it projects firmly from the hub, following the first step with his gaze.
He uses that grip to turn the hub a quarter-turn while his left hand braces its centre, shoulders and head leaning into the small deliberate action.
He folds the blue grip back, then extends the cream triangle grip with his right hand, checking its firm hinge closely.
He turns the supported hub another quarter-turn using the second grip, watching the complete physical movement instead of simply ticking an item.
He unfolds the orange square grip for the final step; it droops at its loose hinge and he pauses with a puzzled raised brow before attempting to force it.
He tilts the hub sideways near his chest and gently lifts the loose orange hinge to inspect it, leaving the first two grips folded and intact.
He lowers the hub to his waist with the orange grip still visibly loose and extended, his right palm open beside the missing executable step, ready to update and retest.

sheets.title: Examine the trust boundary
sheets.purpose: Show systematic threat inspection and preserve an uncovered boundary for mitigation; six visible categories are prompts, not proof of security.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Threat Model Registry preview or after a confirmed threat entry. A mitigated visual requires a confirmed mitigation event and evidence.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8 with the gap visible. Do not close every cover or imply STRIDE coverage proves security.
props: One compact torso-width blue lock-box model, about110px across, with six broad hinged port covers carrying distinct simple shapes; covers remain at least12px across. One orange cover sits slightly ajar and a plain closed shackle is integral.
One thick red blunt wedge with a round handle, explicitly a safe abstract test probe.

slots.beat: Amr supports the six-port model in his left palm near his waist and holds the red blunt wedge low in his right, looking closely at the ajar orange cover.
He raises the box toward his chest and rotates it to expose three different shaped covers, checking the boundary with narrowed, attentive eyes.
He turns the orange cover to the front and bends his head down, bringing the wedge tip level with its existing gap.
He gently inserts only the blunt tip into the visible gap, keeping both hands clearly on their props; his eyebrows rise at the open boundary.
He stops advancing the wedge and lifts his right elbow into a deliberate pause, leaving the shallow entry visible.
He withdraws the wedge completely and props the orange cover open with its own integral hinge, preserving the finding without damage.
He turns the box frontward, orange gap above his supporting palm, while the red wedge remains lowered safely beside his right hip.
He cradles the model and gives a sober open-palm invitation toward the visible gap, ready to record and own the mitigation; no all-secure signal.

sheets.title: Close a finding after the recheck
sheets.purpose: Give a resolved vulnerability a visible verification step rather than removing its warning merely because work was marked done.
sheets.trigger: Play the complete sequence only after a confirmed vulnerability resolution with a recorded recheck; otherwise treat it as an explicitly illustrative procedure preview.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8. Replays start from the illustrative warning state; a real resolved state is shown only on the confirmed event described in the trigger.
props: One blue square test tile made of two captive interlocking halves, with a narrow orange seam and an integral red warning flap.
One thick cream square verification collar with a matching square opening, no lettering.

slots.beat: Amr holds the tile in his left hand with its red flap raised and the empty square collar in his right, looking between them with care.
He brings both to chest height and tilts the tile to inspect its orange seam from the side.
He presses the tile’s two captive halves fully together using both thumbs, keeping the warning flap raised and the collar supported against his palm.
He transfers the joined tile to his right fingers and raises the empty collar upright in his left hand, aligning their square edges.
He pushes the tile carefully through the collar until its entire far edge emerges, his gaze fixed on the clearance.
He draws the tile back out, checks its still-joined seam and gives a small, restrained verification nod.
Only after that visible fit check, he folds the tile’s integral red warning flap flat against its back with his right thumb.
He lowers both the retested tile and collar to his waist, keeping them side by side with a composed expression; no global security celebration.

sheets.title: Keep evidence connected to its control
sheets.purpose: Show an explicit control-to-evidence relationship and leave unsupported control leaves visibly unlinked; no blanket certification.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Compliance Control Map preview or after a confirmed evidence link is saved. Do not imply an audit, framework or regulation is fully satisfied.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8; never auto-link the remaining controls or imply certification.
props: One hinged cream control fan of three broad leaves with simple geometric emblems and large eyelets; an evidence leaf with a matching circle is permanently tethered to the fan by a short loose blue cord.

slots.beat: Amr holds the three-leaf control fan in his left hand and the tethered evidence leaf in his right, their loose blue cord hanging between his hands.
He spreads the control leaves into a shallow fan and lowers his chin to inspect their large empty eyelets.
He raises the evidence leaf beside the circle-marked control leaf, comparing the two visible pictograms with a thoughtful side glance.
He turns the circle control leaf outward and brings its eyelet next to the evidence leaf’s eyelet, bracing them with his left thumb.
He pulls the captive blue cord’s thick end through both adjacent eyelets with his right fingers, keeping the two other control leaves separate.
He draws the cord snug into a simple large retained loop, creating one clearly visible connection without adding checks to the other leaves.
He lifts the linked pair slightly while the two unlinked control leaves remain fanned below, calmly checking the relationship.
He lowers the fan across his waist and offers the single linked pair toward the viewer, attentive and matter-of-fact; the other eyelets stay open.

sheets.title: A focus path must reach the next key
sheets.purpose: Make a keyboard navigation barrier visible and keep the tested focus route distinct from an unverified accessibility pass.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Accessibility Audit Tracker preview. Use the post-fix complete path only after a confirmed resolved issue with keyboard retest.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8 for a confirmed retest or labelled illustrative procedure. Do not infer all WCAG issues are closed.
props: One thick palm-sized keyboard fob with four oversized raised square keys, one with a hinged orange lip that can block the edge.
One blue square focus hoop with a short integral handle.

slots.beat: Amr holds the four-key fob flat in his left palm and places the blue focus hoop around its first key with his right hand, watching closely.
He raises the fob toward chest height and moves the hoop carefully from the first key to the second, keeping its square outline visible.
He tries to move the hoop onto the third key; its edge meets the raised orange lip and his brows lift at the obstruction.
He tilts the fob sideways at waist height and bends his head to inspect the blocked edge from below.
He lifts the hoop clear and folds the orange lip down with his right thumb, a visible physical demonstration of the proposed fix.
He reseats the hoop on the second key and deliberately advances it across the now-flat third key.
He moves the hoop onto the fourth and final key, then checks back along all four keys with a concentrated glance.
He lowers the fob and keeps the hoop around the last key, offering a restrained nod at this specific tested route, with no universal accessibility emblem.

sheets.title: Place the dependency in the landscape
sheets.purpose: Make a value chain and one component’s market-evolution position tangible, without suggesting all components deserve the same investment.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Wardley Map Canvas preview or after a confirmed component/link edit. No build-versus-buy decision is claimed.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8; component positions remain a map illustration, not an automatic procurement recommendation.

One tethered chain of three large coloured component rings, joined by two short cream links.

He opens the ladder’s rounded feet with his right fingers while his left hand holds its top; the short linked ring chain hangs visibly from his curled left fingers until the frame is supported below his chest.
He hooks the chain’s top blue ring near the upper person emblem, his right hand raised while his left supports the frame.
He lets the next orange ring hang to the lower left rung and looks down along the short visible dependency link.
He lifts the bottom teal ring with his right fingers and slides it sideways onto the lower right rung, keeping both connecting links visible.
He tilts the frame toward himself and traces the physical chain from the top need to the lowest component with his eyes, not a pointer.
He turns the ladder a little frontward, showing the lower rings at distinct left and right positions instead of collapsing them together.
He rests the compact ladder in both palms at waist height and settles with a thoughtful, evaluating expression, the whole value chain still connected.

sheets.title: Compare like with like
sheets.purpose: Show how a shared benchmark exposes a small mismatch that a broad model score can hide.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative LLM Eval Tracker preview, or after a confirmed eval comparison/regression. Do not invent a measured regression from a page visit.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8; do not grow the short tooth or celebrate a benchmark pass.

One purple result comb strip with the same width and origin notch but a visibly shorter third tooth.

He raises both strips closer to his chest and rotates them so their teeth point in the same direction.
He brings their large origin notches together with both thumbs, carefully aligning the left ends.
He overlaps the strips almost completely and leans his head right, looking along the row of teeth.
He slides the purple strip downward by a small distance while keeping the origins aligned, exposing the shortened third tooth as a clear step.
He presses a right fingertip gently against that short tooth, his lips pursed in a concerned verification expression.
He separates the strips just enough to show both origins and the single mismatch, keeping all other teeth visibly comparable.
He holds the pair parallel at waist height and offers a measured open glance toward the viewer, preserving the mismatch for investigation instead of a pass sign.

sheets.title: Review the next version before release
sheets.purpose: Keep prompt versions physically distinguishable and show a draft entering review while the existing production version remains protected.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Prompt Registry preview or after a confirmed draft/review event. A production transition requires a separately confirmed promotion event.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8 with the green base closed and draft still exposed. Do not auto-promote a prompt to production.
props: One short telescoping catalogue with three permanently nested cream sleeves: a deep closed green base, a blue middle sleeve and an orange outer draft sleeve, each carrying only a simple shape emblem.
One broad blue review collar.

slots.beat: Amr holds the closed nested catalogue horizontally in both hands with the blue review collar parked around its far end; the orange outer sleeve faces his gaze and the green base stays sealed.
He pulls the orange sleeve outward with his right fingers, revealing the blue middle sleeve while his left hand retains the green base.
He rotates the extended orange sleeve a quarter-turn and tilts his head down to inspect its simple large emblem.
He slides it back only halfway, leaving the newest orange version distinctly visible rather than burying it in the green base.
He takes the blue review collar from its retained resting place at the catalogue’s end and opens it with his right thumb.
He seats that collar around the exposed orange sleeve next to the blue middle sleeve, marking this version for review.
He turns the catalogue upright against his left palm and checks that the green base remains closed beneath the reviewed draft.
He holds the partly extended catalogue beside his lower chest with a patient attentive smile, ready for review; no release or deprecation claim.

sheets.title: Specify the fallback before the drop
sheets.purpose: Make an AI feature’s fallback and controlled recovery part of its design before testing a risky path.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative AI Feature Spec preview or after a confirmed specification save; no AI call, launch, reliability result or delivered feature is implied.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8. Repeat only the short hand-height demonstration; no falling character, flight effects or implied production deployment.
props: One small blue hollow model crate with a broad circular model emblem and a large integral orange fallback handle folded against one side.
One short cream safety tether with a large rounded loop at each end; no hooks or sharp details.

slots.beat: Amr cups the blue crate in his left palm and holds the coiled cream tether in his right, looking down with a designing, curious expression.
He raises the crate to lower-chest height and unfolds its orange fallback handle with his right thumb.
He threads one large tether loop through that handle and folds the loop back over itself, keeping the attachment simple and visible.
He slips the tether’s other loop around two right fingers and gently pulls his hands apart to check the connection.
He lowers his left palm a short distance so the crate hangs only just below his right hand on the taut tether, watching it closely.
He swings his left palm directly beneath the crate and lets the orange handle guide it back into that open supporting hand.
He relaxes the tether into a loose coil beside the supported crate and inspects the still-attached fallback handle.
He holds the small crate and coiled tether together at waist height with a modest ready nod, presenting the prepared safety path as a specification metaphor.

sheets.title: Give the claim an evidence footing
sheets.purpose: Remind the viewer to attach verifiable support to a claim rather than make an unsupported answer look authoritative.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Hallucination Log preview. A grounded-claim outcome may reflect a confirmed source attachment/correction event, never the mere presence of the tool.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8 as an evidence-link illustration. Never add a universal truth badge, fabricate a source or imply that a visual match verifies a factual claim.
props: One tall slim cream claim tile with a large blue circle pictogram and an intentionally narrow lower edge.
One broad amber U-shaped evidence footing, its inner notch matching the tile’s blue-circle base tab; no writing.

slots.beat: Amr holds the slim claim tile upright on his left palm and the separate amber footing in his right, watching the tile’s precarious narrow edge.
He loosens his supporting left fingers; the tile tips slightly and he raises his brows in a small concerned O, keeping his right hand ready.
He catches the tile safely across his left palm and brings the empty amber footing closer for inspection.

He holds the amber evidence footing in his anatomical RIGHT hand and the cream claim tile in his anatomical LEFT hand. Keeping both hands visibly occupied with those two props, he raises the footing slightly to inspect its notch and looks between notch and tile. His mouth is thoughtful; neither hand touches his face or chin. Exactly two arms and two hands.
He slides the tile’s lower tab into the U-shaped footing using both thumbs, making the support conspicuous rather than hiding it.
He stands the supported pair upright in his left palm and briefly lifts his right fingertips away to test the wider physical footing.
He turns his left palm slightly toward the viewer while his right open hand frames the visible evidence bracket beneath the claim.
He lowers the grounded assembly to waist height and settles with a careful closed smile, the amber support remaining at least as visible as the claim tile.

sheets.title: Notice spend before the next token
sheets.purpose: Give finite token spend a visible budget boundary and encourage checking the next increment before crossing it.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Token-Cost Tracker preview or after a confirmed usage entry. Coin positions are a metaphor, never fabricated spend data or a billing claim.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8. Never loop by spawning extra discs, reset a real budget, or imply that estimated spend is a confirmed charge.
props: One squat clear jar with a broad amber budget band around its upper third, no numbers or labels.
One set of six large flat blue token discs with simple central circular holes; the same six discs persist throughout.

slots.beat: Amr holds the clear jar in his left hand at his waist with three discs visibly inside and three stacked in his open right palm.
He lifts the jar toward his chest and compares the existing disc stack with the broad amber band, his gaze moving upward.
He picks up the top loose disc with his right thumb and forefinger while balancing the other two against his curled fingers.
He brings that one disc above the jar mouth and pauses with a cautious side glance at the remaining gap beneath the budget band.
He lowers the disc through the mouth onto the existing stack; four discs now sit inside, with two still in his right hand.
He tilts the jar a little frontward so the increased stack and amber boundary remain visible together.
He raises the next loose disc toward the mouth, then stops short and draws it back to his chest with a deliberate thinking expression.
He lowers both hands to waist height, jar of four in the left and two unspent discs in the right, calmly pausing before the next increment.

sheets.title: Measure the trade-offs on both sides
sheets.purpose: Encourage a like-for-like comparison of model trade-offs while leaving the choice open.
sheets.trigger: Illustrative Model Comparison Matrix preview or after a confirmed comparison entry. No winner, benchmark result or provider capability is inferred.
sheets.loop: Hold frame 8. A chosen-model state belongs only to a separately confirmed decision, not this neutral comparison.
props: One hinged specimen with a broad short blue arm and a narrower taller purple arm, each carrying a distinct simple shape emblem and three large measuring shoulders.
One cream two-jaw sliding caliper with blunt ends and no numbers.

slots.beat: Amr holds the closed hinged specimen in his left hand and the blunt caliper in his right, looking between their shapes with interest.
He opens the blue and purple candidate arms into a wide V at waist height so their different proportions are obvious.
He raises the blue arm beside his lower chest and slides the caliper jaws around its broad first shoulder, leaning his head toward the contact.
He lifts the caliper free without changing its opening and brings it across to the purple arm’s corresponding shoulder.
He notices the spare width around the narrower purple shoulder and raises one brow, holding the gauge visibly level rather than choosing a winner.
He rotates the specimen a quarter-turn and opens the caliper wider to compare the candidates along their second, differently proportioned dimension.
He returns both arms frontward in the same V and rests the caliper across their base, letting both contrasting profiles remain visible.
He lowers the balanced specimen and gauge to his waist and opens his right palm in a thoughtful trade-off gesture, neither candidate raised as a winner.

sheets.title: An open check stays visible
sheets.purpose: Show that launch readiness requires evidence for every claimed check, and that an unresolved item remains visibly open.

sheets.loop: Hold frame 8 with the amber latch open. Do not snap it shut or flash an all-safe outcome without a confirmed evidence-backed event.

One plain blue square evidence block that can be inspected beside the open latch but is not automatically fitted.

slots.beat: Amr supports the review case in his left palm and holds the separate evidence block in his right, looking down at the single amber open latch.
He tilts the case toward his chest and runs his left thumb slowly along its four visibly closed latches.
He reaches the amber latch and tries only a gentle fingertip press; it stays open, and he pauses with a serious raised brow.
He opens the case lid a little at that corner so the unresolved gap is clear, supporting the other end with his left fingers.
He lifts the blue evidence block to eye level and turns it in his right fingers, examining both its plain faces thoughtfully.
He brings the block beside the open latch for comparison but keeps a clear gap between them, withholding an unsupported closure.
He lowers the block into his right palm and turns the case frontward, leaving the amber latch conspicuously raised.
He holds the partly open case at waist height with a calm wait gesture, ready to request the missing evidence before a launch decision.

sheets.title: Try the new model in a small lane
sheets.purpose: Show a candidate model taking a limited canary slot while the established model and rollback path remain available.

sheets.loop: Hold frame 8. Never multiply the canary pegs or remove the established module without a separately confirmed rollout/retirement event.

One large cream canary peg with a simple small-circle emblem, no percentage text.

slots.beat: Amr holds the twin-slot dock across his left palm with the cream canary peg in his right fingers, examining both retained modules.
He tilts the dock upward so the blue established module and its occupied main socket are clearly visible, his expression steady.
He hinges the purple candidate module out a little with his right thumb, exposing its separate small test socket.

slots.beat: Stand holding a single short cable at waist height; its two rounded unplugged ends and one loose figure-eight crossover are visible.
Support the lower loop in the left palm and inspect where one cable end passes through the crossover.
Open the upper loop gently with the right thumb and forefinger while the left hand prevents the cable from dropping.
Feed one broad cable end back through the opened loop, keeping the entire cable visibly continuous.
Draw the freed ends apart only slightly until the crossover disappears and the cable forms one relaxed U.
Wind the cable into two large even loops around the open left palm using the right hand.
Wrap the soft reusable strap around the middle of the completed coil and press its ends together.
Hold up the compact secured coil at waist height, with both rounded end caps visible and no plugs inserted anywhere.

sheets.title: Fold, fly and catch
sheets.purpose: A short paper-flight surprise with a complete visible return.
sheets.trigger: Explicit gallery play or optional user-requested easter egg in normal motion.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. Every airborne pose stays inside the cell. A new replay begins from its own initial flat sheet rather than a magical mid-loop unfolding.
props: one broad plain square paper sheet folded into a simple plane

slots.beat: Stand holding one flat plain paper sheet in both hands at waist height, its full outline visible.
Fold the sheet lengthwise, left hand stabilising one edge while the right hand presses the central crease.
Bring the two upper corners inward to form a broad simple nose, keeping both hands separated.
Fold one broad wing outward while the left hand supports the centre crease.
Finish the second wing and hold the complete paper plane by its underside at chest height.
Release the plane with a gentle forward-and-slightly-upward push; its nose remains within the same cell, just beyond his open hand.
Catch the returning descending plane lightly between both hands below chest level, eyes following its body.
Hold the intact plane horizontally in both palms at waist height with a small pleased smile.

sheets.title: The yo-yo comes home
sheets.purpose: A precise gravity-and-string toy journey with a calm catch.
sheets.trigger: Explicit optional play in normal motion; no unsolicited looping near content.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. No endless yo-yo motion; an explicit replay is required.
props: one large rounded yo-yo
one short thick readable string with a single finger loop

slots.beat: Stand with the large yo-yo resting in the open right palm at waist height; its short string is safely wound around the axle.
Secure the small string loop loosely around the right middle finger while the left fingertips steady the toy.
Move the left hand away and tilt the right palm downward, preparing one gentle release.
Let the yo-yo descend on its straight visible string to just above knee height, right elbow comfortably bent.
Hold the right hand still as the yo-yo turns at the string's lower end, both feet planted.
Give one small upward wrist movement, starting the yo-yo's visible return along the same string.
Catch the returning yo-yo softly in the right palm; the string is rewound around its axle.
Cup the captured toy with both hands at waist height and relax the finger loop without pulling it tight.

sheets.title: Set the top spinning, then stop it
sheets.purpose: A small contained spin with deliberate retrieval instead of permanent background movement.
sheets.trigger: Explicit optional play in normal motion; never automatic after a visitor stops animations.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. Spin never repeats without an explicit replay and cannot move outside its tray.
props: one broad wooden spinning top with rounded stem
small shallow rimmed spinning tray

slots.beat: Stand supporting the small rimmed tray on the left palm; the wooden top rests still in its centre.
Pinch the top's short rounded stem with right thumb and forefinger while keeping the left palm level.
Rotate the pinched stem gently to prepare the release, eyes focused on the centre of the tray.
Release the top upright; right fingertips lift clear while the top spins in the tray centre.
Watch the top lean slightly as it begins to slow, keeping the tray level and both feet still.
Cup the right fingers loosely around the slowing top to stop it gently within the rim.
Lift the now-still top by its stem and rest its base in the right palm.
Show the still top in the right palm beside the empty tray in the left, with a relaxed satisfied expression.

sheets.title: Gather the rolling pencils
sheets.purpose: A miniature containment puzzle where several rolling objects are gathered with care.
sheets.trigger: Explicit gallery play; a neutral tactile scene, never triggered as a judgement about messy work.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. The pencils never fall to the floor and are not repeatedly scattered.
props: three short chunky capped pencils with blunt ends
small shallow V-shaped pencil channel
wide-mouthed compact pencil cup

slots.beat: Stand supporting a shallow V-shaped channel at waist height in the left hand; three chunky blunt pencils rest across it and a small cup is fixed at one end.
Notice one pencil beginning to roll sideways toward the channel lip, gaze attentive rather than alarmed.
Place the side of the open right hand gently along the lip to stop the rolling pencil inside the channel.
Use two right fingertips to bring the second pencil parallel to the first, keeping both supported.
Align the third pencil beside the others so their three blunt ends form a clear row.
Tip the channel a small controlled amount toward its attached wide-mouthed cup while the right hand guides the ends.
Slide all three pencils together into the cup and stop the channel before any pencil can fall.
Hold the now-contained three pencils upright in the cup, both hands supporting the small assembly at waist level.

sheets.title: Measure, then guide the return
sheets.purpose: A satisfying controlled extension and recoil of a retractable object.
sheets.trigger: Explicit optional play in normal motion; no measurements of the visitor or their work.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. No snapping recoil, whiplash, repeated extension or off-cell tape.
props: compact rounded tape-measure case
short broad blank tape with a large soft end tab

slots.beat: Stand holding the closed tape-measure case in the left hand at waist height; the soft end tab rests against its mouth.
Grip the large soft end tab with the right thumb and forefinger, keeping hands comfortably apart.
Pull a short broad length of tape horizontally to the right, no wider than his shoulder span.
Press the case lock with the left thumb and relax the right grip slightly; the extended tape remains steady.
Look along the held tape with a curious small smile; its surface is plain, without readable numbers.
Release the lock with the left thumb while keeping the right hand firmly on the soft tab.
Guide the tape slowly back toward the case with the right hand, shortening it without a snap.
Seat the soft tab against the case mouth and hold the complete compact tool in both hands.

sheets.title: The keystone holds
sheets.purpose: A quiet construction reveal: a small arch stands after the supporting form is removed.
sheets.trigger: Explicit optional tactile play; never claims a team's dependencies or architecture are solved.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. No collapse, rebuilding loop or magical multiplication of blocks.
props: five broad lightweight wooden arch blocks including one clear keystone
compact removable rounded arch former
compact narrow waist-height pedestal with a plain support base

slots.beat: Stand beside a compact narrow pedestal whose support base is at waist height; five broad wooden blocks and a rounded former are visibly grouped on it.
Set the rounded former upright on the base with the left hand while the right hand steadies its foot.
Place the two left arch blocks against the former, keeping the outer block supported with left fingertips.
Place the two right arch blocks symmetrically, right fingertips holding the outer block stable.
Lower the single wedge-shaped keystone into the top gap using both thumbs and forefingers.
Take both hands away briefly to show the completed arch still resting around the former.
Slide the former carefully forward out of the arch with one hand while the other hovers nearby without touching the blocks.
Hold the removed former beside the standing five-block arch and look at the stable result with a modest pleased smile.

sheets.title: A little toy can wait
sheets.purpose: A mechanical toy surprise with an unhurried, visible pause and restart under Amr's hand.
sheets.trigger: Explicit optional gallery play in normal motion. Do not run this sequence when real reduced motion or animation pause is active.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. No endless walking, escape, actual companion-pause acknowledgement or restart without an explicit play request.
props: small rounded clockwork beetle toy with a broad visible stop paddle
large fixed winding key
short shallow rimmed toy tray

slots.beat: Stand supporting the rimmed tray in the left hand; the clockwork beetle rests still in its centre with its broad stop paddle upright.
Turn the large fixed winding key once with the right thumb and forefinger while the left hand steadies the tray.
Place the right index finger gently on the broad stop paddle, keeping the wound toy still.
Lift the finger away to let the toy move a short distance along the tray, entirely inside the rim.
Press the broad stop paddle again with one finger so the toy visibly pauses before reaching the tray end.
Hold the toy paused for a calm beat, eyes on the mechanism and no impatient expression.
Keep the stop paddle depressed while lifting the toy into the right palm, preventing an uncontrolled restart.
Present the now-still toy in the right palm beside the empty tray, winding key and stop paddle both visible.

sheets.title: A paper flake follows the balloon
sheets.purpose: A contained static-attraction surprise with a visible cause and release.
sheets.trigger: Explicit optional easter egg in normal motion; no interaction with the visitor's pointer or content.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. No permanent attraction loop or flake multiplication.
props: one small matte red balloon with short closed knot and no string
one folded dark wool cloth
one large plain rounded-corner cream rectangular paper flake
one shallow tray
one compact waist-high pedestal with visible stem and stable foot

slots.beat: Stand beside the single shallow tray resting securely on its visible waist-high pedestal, stem and foot shown. Hold ONE small matte red balloon in LEFT hand and ONE folded dark wool cloth in RIGHT. ONE oversized plain cream rectangular paper flake rests alone in the tray; no cutout shapes or scraps.

Rub the same balloon gently with the same folded cloth below shoulder level. Both hands are occupied, so the TRAY remains on the unchanged VISIBLE pedestal. The ONE plain paper flake stays in the tray, plainly visible. No hair or clothing changes.

Set the one folded cloth on the tray left side. Hold balloon in LEFT hand just above the ONE rectangular flake at tray centre, RIGHT hand now empty beside tray. Tray, pedestal stem and foot remain visible and supported.

Keep balloon steady in LEFT hand and watch the ONE plain rectangular flake lift a short distance above the tray toward the balloon, with a small visible air gap beneath the flake. RIGHT hand open nearby. This one flake alone may be briefly airborne; tray and stand never float. Cloth stays on tray.

Hold balloon in LEFT hand with the ONE plain rectangular flake lightly adhered to its side. Show the whole tray on its pedestal beside him; the tray now has cloth but NO second paper flake. RIGHT hand open and empty near balloon. Quiet curious expression.

Keep balloon in LEFT hand and detach the SAME ONE rectangular flake with RIGHT thumb and forefinger. Exactlyone flake, no white copies or small particles. Tray and folded cloth remain on the visible unchanged pedestal.
Lower that SAME ONE plain rectangular flake into the tray with RIGHT fingertips while LEFT holds balloon clearly separate. Tray, cloth, pedestal stem and foot remain visible, no floating hardware.

Rest balloon securely within the tray rim beside the ONE plain rectangular flake and ONE folded cloth. Show BOTH empty open hands lifted clear, proving everything is supported by the tray and its visible pedestal. Entire stem and broad stable foot remain within the cell; no extra flakes, balloon or cloth.

sheets.title: The block stays standing
sheets.purpose: A harmless miniature inertia trick with a failed slow test and a controlled successful pull.
sheets.trigger: Explicit gallery play in normal motion; not a task-completion animation or performance challenge.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. The quick-pull beat is omitted under reduced motion; no spontaneous reset or repeated challenge.
props: compact stable waist-height pedestal
small short cloth with one broad gripping edge
one squat rounded wooden toy block

slots.beat: Stand beside a stable compact pedestal; a short cloth lies on top with one squat wooden block centred on it.
Grip the cloth's broad hanging edge with both hands, knees and elbows relaxed.
Pull very slowly a short distance; the wooden block visibly moves with the cloth toward the pedestal centre-front.
Stop the pull before the block approaches an edge, lift one hand and look thoughtfully at the moved block.
Reposition the block safely at the pedestal centre and smooth the cloth flat with the other hand.
Grip the short cloth edge again and give one quick level pull, keeping his hands and the cloth within the cell.
Hold the removed cloth in both hands while the squat wooden block remains upright at the pedestal centre.
Fold the removed cloth once over his left hand and inspect the still-standing block with a small pleased smile.

sheets.title: Find the little release tab
sheets.purpose: A tactile surprise where the useful move is releasing pressure rather than pulling harder.
sheets.trigger: Explicit optional gallery play; never triggered as commentary on the visitor's decisions or effort.
sheets.loop: One shot; hold8. No harder-pulling loop, sudden fall, recoil into the face or automatic reattachment.
props: oversized soft suction cup with a broad rounded release tab and short handle
smooth thick circular puck supported on a small compact stand

slots.beat: Stand beside the smooth puck at waist height, holding the soft suction cup by its short handle in the right hand.
Press the cup flat onto the puck with the right palm while the left hand steadies the puck edge.
Give one gentle outward tug on the handle; the cup remains attached and the puck stays stable.
Stop tugging immediately, relax the right elbow and look toward the cup's broad release tab.
Hold the handle lightly with the right hand and pinch the broad release tab using left thumb and forefinger.
Lift the tab just enough to break the seal; the cup's rim visibly peels from one edge.
Catch the released cup securely in the right hand and move it a short distance clear of the puck.
Present the separate intact cup and clean puck side by side, both hands relaxed and the large release tab visible.
